modify.note: Update the producer service (WebhookTaskerProducerService) to depend on WebhookTasker instead of InternalTasker and pass its existing payloads through `deliverWebhook`. Preserve the tasker framework's established dispatch and error behavior so the producer does not invent a separate fallback policy or accidentally deliver a webhook twice. Keep payload construction and actual delivery semantics (WebhookTaskConsumer) shared across both modes.

add_nodes.label: Webhook tasker
add_nodes.summary: WebhookTasker choosing a synchronous or Trigger.dev implementation of IWebhookTasker by environment.
add_nodes.description: WebhookTasker extends the Tasker base class with a WebhookSyncTasker (calls WebhookTaskConsumer directly) and a WebhookTriggerTasker (triggers a Trigger.dev webhook job), selected through ENABLE_ASYNC_TASKER.
add_nodes.note: New WebhookTasker: route webhook delivery through a WebhookTasker that uses the same environment-based dispatch pattern as the existing taskers. Define the shared `IWebhookTasker` contract around the existing WebhookTaskPayload and `{ taskId }` result, then supply synchronous and Trigger.dev implementations to the Tasker base class. Use `ENABLE_ASYNC_TASKER` through that common mechanism so production can enqueue work while an environment without async task processing can complete delivery immediately. WebhookSyncTasker calls the injected WebhookTaskConsumer directly and awaits its work, returning an identifier through the same result shape. WebhookTriggerTasker dynamically loads and triggers the webhook job and returns the queued task's identifier. The Trigger.dev job should validate the same payload schema, resolve the consumer through the existing dependency-injection container, and execute the same delivery operation. Keep payload construction and actual delivery semantics shared across both modes. Wire the Trigger.dev job configuration and schema re-export. Add the corresponding DI tokens and modules using the project's binding pattern.
